end.parentNote: Kabir practised taking-away stories with stars, rotis, kites, buses, and children, and used backward steps on a number line. They correctly worked through examples such as 7 − 2 = 5, 6 − 1 = 5, 9 − 4 = 5, and 5 − 2 = 3. Kabir mixed up subtraction order once, saying 3 − 5 could make 2; this was not corrected by the last time it appeared. At home, use small objects to act out “3 take away 5” and discuss why there are not 5 objects to remove.
